title: FBI Launches Probe Into 2022 Dobbs Leak to Intimidate Journalists
description_short: FBI Launches Probe Into 2022 Dobbs Leak to Intimidate Journalists
description_medium: On May 26, 2025, FBI Deputy Director Dan Bongino announced that the bureau was reopening its investigation into the 2022 leak of the Supreme Court’s draft Dobbs opinion to Politico. Reporters Without Borders and 11 press freedom groups later warned that the probe could chill journalism. Their letter described the investigation as an attempt to stifle reporting; that motive is an attributed criticism, not an established finding.
description_long: On May 26, 2025, FBI Deputy Director Dan Bongino announced that the bureau was reopening its investigation into who leaked the Supreme Court’s 2022 draft Dobbs opinion to Politico. The probe came about three years after the document became public. On June 3, Reporters Without Borders and 11 press freedom groups wrote to FBI Director Kash Patel and Bongino to object. They warned that investigating the disclosure could intimidate reporters and chill journalism, arguing that sharing an unpublished court decision is not itself prohibited by law. Reporters Without Borders also connected the renewed probe to Patel’s earlier pledge to “come after people in the media.” Those statements describe the groups’ concern and their reading of the investigation’s implications; they do not independently establish the FBI’s purpose or resolve whether any separate offense was committed. The supplied reporting supports the announcement and the press groups’ response, but the title presents intimidation as the bureau’s intent. The linked account does not establish that motive. A fuller record of the investigation’s stated legal basis and any targets or charges would be needed to settle the issue.
notes: Reason: The supplied facts support a reopened leak investigation and press-group criticism, but do not establish that the FBI launched it to intimidate journalists.
Proposed correction: “FBI Reopens Investigation Into 2022 Dobbs Draft Leak; Press Groups Warn of Chilling Effect.”

title: Trump Reverses Title IX Transgender Protections Via 'Dear Colleague' Letter
description_short: Trump Reverses Title IX Transgender Protections Via 'Dear Colleague' Letter
description_medium: On January 31, 2025, the Department of Education issued a “Dear Colleague” letter directing schools to return to the 2020 Title IX rules. The letter said open investigations should immediately use that framework, ending Biden-era protections for transgender students described in the account. The cited Reuters link concerns transgender participation in sports, not the letter, so it does not verify these details.
description_long: On January 31, 2025, the Department of Education issued a “Dear Colleague” letter directing schools to return to the 2020 Title IX regulations. Acting Assistant Secretary Craig Trainor cited President Trump’s executive order defining sex in binary biological terms as the legal basis. The department also directed that open Title IX investigations be “immediately reoriented” to the earlier framework. The supplied account says this change removed protections for transgender students, including the ability to use facilities aligned with their gender identity, and affected an estimated 1.6 million students in K–12 schools and higher education. Those are substantial claims about the letter’s scope and effect, but the linked Reuters report is about the administration’s policy on transgender women and girls in sports. It does not appear to document the January 31 letter or the cited enrollment estimate. The event can be described as a reported change in Title IX enforcement, but the linked source does not substantiate its details. A source for the letter itself or reporting specifically about it is needed before treating the estimated reach and particular protections as verified.
notes: Reason: The linked Reuters article concerns transgender participation in sports rather than the January 31 Title IX letter; the letter’s text and the 1.6 million estimate are not substantiated by that source.
Proposed correction: Replace the sports-policy link with the original January 31, 2025 “Dear Colleague” letter or reporting specifically documenting it.

title: Trans Military Ban Reinstated via Executive Order 14183
description_short: Trans Military Ban Reinstated via Executive Order 14183
description_medium: On January 27, 2025, Donald Trump signed Executive Order 14183, reinstating restrictions on transgender military service. The order revoked Biden’s prior directive, called transgender identity inconsistent with military service, and directed facilities to be separated by sex. The supplied account says several thousand serving troops could face discharge; it does not say they had already been discharged.
description_long: On January 27, 2025, Donald Trump signed Executive Order 14183, titled “Prioritizing Military Excellence and Readiness.” The order reinstated restrictions on transgender service members and revoked President Biden’s Executive Order 14004. It said that being transgender conflicted with a soldier’s commitment to an “honorable, truthful and disciplined lifestyle” and described pronoun use as inconsistent with humility and selflessness. The order also directed that sleeping and bathroom facilities be separated by sex. The White House fact sheet confirms the order’s principal changes to service standards, pronoun guidance and facilities. The supplied account estimates that several thousand transgender service members could face discharge, and says NCLR and GLAD Law filed suit on behalf of six active-duty members within a day. Those details describe potential consequences and an immediate legal challenge; they do not establish how many people were ultimately discharged or how the cases were resolved. The action therefore changed federal military policy and placed currently serving members at risk, while the individual outcomes remained pending in the supplied account.

title: Alien Enemies Act Invoked; 261 Deported to CECOT Defying Court Order
description_short: Alien Enemies Act Invoked; 261 Deported to CECOT Defying Court Order
description_medium: On March 15, 2025, Donald Trump invoked the Alien Enemies Act against Venezuelan gang Tren de Aragua, calling its activity an “invasion.” The next day, Judge James Boasberg ordered deportations halted, including flights already underway. The administration proceeded to send 261 people to El Salvador’s CECOT prison, later arguing the order did not apply after the planes left U.S. airspace.
description_long: On March 15, 2025, Trump invoked the Alien Enemies Act of 1798 — last used during World War II — against Venezuelan gang Tren de Aragua, declaring it an 'invasion.' The following evening, U.S. District Judge James Boasberg issued a temporary restraining order blocking deportations and verbally ordered planes already in the air to turn back; the administration defied both the verbal and written order, arguing planes had left U.S. airspace before the written ruling at 7:26 PM. A total of 261 people were deported that day — 137 under the Alien Enemies Act and 23 alleged MS-13 members — and transferred to El Salvador's CECOT mega-prison at $6 million per year paid to President Bukele. The administration's top lawyers signed a court filing arguing the order 'did not apply' because deportees had already left U.S. territory. Legal experts and three Supreme Court justices warned the government's logic would allow deportation of any person, including U.S. citizens, to foreign prisons without legal consequence as long as it was done before a court could intervene.

title: Crypto Pardon Economy: Executives Buy Clemency Through Trump Ties
description_short: Crypto Pardon Economy: Executives Buy Clemency Through Trump Ties
description_medium: An August 2025 New York Times report described Binance founder Changpeng Zhao’s campaign for a presidential pardon, including lobbyists and a business deal. The supplied account also links pardons for Zhao, Arthur Hayes and Ross Ulbricht to Trump-family crypto interests. The linked article predates Zhao’s reported October pardon and cannot establish that investments or business ties secured clemency.
description_long: An August 2025 New York Times report described Binance founder Changpeng Zhao’s campaign for a presidential pardon, referring to lobbyists and a business deal. The account also names BitMEX co-founder Arthur Hayes and Silk Road founder Ross Ulbricht as crypto figures Trump pardoned in 2025, and says Ulbricht’s release fulfilled a campaign promise to Bitcoin advocates. It connects Zhao’s later pardon to Binance’s work on the Trump family’s World Liberty Financial stablecoin. These events raise questions about how presidential clemency intersected with political support and crypto business relationships. But the linked Times article was published before Zhao’s stated October 23 pardon, and its title describes a campaign for clemency rather than proof that a business relationship purchased it. The supplied facts also do not show that investing in Trump-linked ventures provided legal protection or caused any of the pardons. The title asserts that executives bought clemency through Trump ties; that causal claim remains unsupported by the linked report. A reliable chronology and evidence connecting a specific pardon decision to a financial benefit are needed to support that conclusion.
notes: Reason: The linked August 2025 article predates Zhao’s reported October pardon, and the supplied facts do not establish that financial ties bought clemency or provided legal protection.
Proposed correction: Narrow the title to the documented pardon events and report the alleged links as questions unless evidence connects them to the decisions.
